title: Choose Voyager's visual world
question: The roll assigned Consignment Manifest. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Consignment Manifest
options.lineage: freight consignment notes, container stencils, wharf checker plate
options.thesis: Every person, cost and journey is a consigned item with an origin, a destination, a carrier and a weight.
options.viewport: Trip name stencilled across the head plate; the two answers stamped as full-width rows -- NEXT MOVEMENT and YOUR BALANCE; then six numbered manifest lines, each with its live count hard-right in a tabular column.
options.risk: Industrial language reads cold for a mates' holiday if the stencils turn decorative instead of functional.

raised.raise: Each trip's stencil colour derives from one stable seed, its invite code, while every money colour stays fixed -- the identity varies, the meaning never does.
One change propagates visibly across the whole sheet: removing a member re-settles every dependent figure in a single orchestrated motion instead of leaving it to be discovered.
The field stays achromatic ink-on-kraft so the one safety-yellow signal is the only chromatic thing on screen and cannot be missed.

options.label: The Lineup Bill
options.lineage: festival lineup grids, screenprint bills, laminates and woven wristbands
options.thesis: The trip is a lineup: days are columns, agreed plans are set times, and your laminate is your membership.
options.viewport: The trip name as a headline bill, today's column pulled forward with agreed items as set times, and your laminate strip pinned along the bottom edge carrying your balance.
options.risk: Also exactly where most concepts for this audience land, and it can read as a festival app rather than a trip planner.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.lineage: a small aircraft's night instrument six-pack
options.thesis: Six instruments, each owning one truth, read in a practiced cross-check sweep.
options.viewport: Two ranked rows of three gauges; next movement and your balance carry trend as well as value, and deviations tilt before anything alarms.
options.risk: A dark instrument panel can read as a car-nerd product rather than something four friends share.
options.case: The strongest fuse of the six: 'a fixed constellation of instruments, each owning one truth' describes your six-tile overview almost literally, and a gauge showing trend beats a static count. Matte black with luminous markings also suits the real late-night scene. Loses only on audience identification -- night aviation is not this cohort's ritual.

options.label: Co-op Cabinet
options.lineage: pixel-art arcade cabinet screens, scanlines and phosphor bloom
options.thesis: The trip as a co-op cabinet: everyone on one screen, and palette law carries every state.
options.viewport: Phosphor-black field, trip name in 8x8 caps pinned to the top edge, six tiles as sprite panels with their counts set as score digits.
options.risk: Scanlines behind a money ledger cost legibility exactly where this product cannot afford to lose it.
options.case: Wins audience identification outright -- arcade nostalgia is native to 18-35 -- and its palette-law state encoding is a genuinely disciplined system. Loses clarity: 8x8 caps cannot carry expense rows or long member names, and integer scaling fights a fluid phone layout.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: One face at five sizes, so the number you actually need is the biggest thing on the page.
options.viewport: Your balance set as a coarse bitmap headline at poster scale, with the expense manifest below it in a fine grotesk at four descending steps.
options.risk: Justified specimen columns and whole-pixel scaling fight a one-handed phone.
options.case: Holds audience identification through the live Y2K revival, and specimen scale-stepping genuinely suits a product with one dominant number per screen. Loses clarity on dense rows and on responsive behaviour.

options.label: Parametric Identity
options.thesis: Each trip reseeds its own identity from its invite code.
options.viewport: A parametric mark reseeded per trip, its palette spilling outward into every control and divider.
options.risk: A palette that varies per trip makes money colours mean different things in different trips.
options.case: Fails product clarity outright for an Operate surface. Someone opens this twenty times a day and needs owed and owing to be the same colour every single time.
options.kept: Systemic derivation from a single seed.

options.label: Deployable Sheet
options.thesis: The trip folds from a hand-sized packet into one rigid tessellated field.
options.viewport: A compact packet that deploys in one pull into a tessellated itinerary field of linked crease cells.
options.risk: Fold interactions are the wrong cost to charge someone using this one-handed at midnight.
options.case: Loses both axes. Miura folding is an aerospace reference this audience does not hold, and 'misfolded' and 'collapsed' are not states this product has.
options.kept: One control propagating visibly across the entire structure.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.lineage: diffracting cloud edges and spectral banding
options.thesis: Colour lives only at the edges while the reading field stays achromatic.
options.viewport: A near-white field with pastel spectral hairlines marking whichever band is active.
options.risk: Pastel hairlines cannot carry money states and fail the contrast this product needs at night.
options.case: Loses both axes. Atmospheric optics is nobody's ritual here, and low-contrast pastels break the accessibility floor PRODUCT.md records for one-handed, low-light, late-night use.
options.kept: Strict restraint in where colour is permitted to live at all.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a trip-planning app ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A hero destination photograph, rounded summary cards, and a tab bar exactly where a visitor expects them.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other travel app, by design.
